The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({e}^{-x}+{x}^{3}-2x)^{′}=-{e}^{-x}+3{x}^{2}-2.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{-{x}_{n}}+{x}_{n}^{3}-2{x}_{n}}{-{e}^{-{x}_{n}}+3{x}_{n}^{2}-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{-{x}_{0}}+{x}_{0}^{3}-2{x}_{0}}{-{e}^{-{x}_{0}}+3{x}_{0}^{2}-2} \\  & =0.5-\frac{{e}^{-0.5}+{0.5}^{3}-2\cdot 0.5}{-{e}^{-0.5}+3\cdot {0.5}^{2}-2} \\  & ≈0.355,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({e}^{2x}+3{x}^{2})^{′}=2{e}^{2x}+6x.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{2{x}_{n}}+3{x}_{n}^{2}-2}{2{e}^{2{x}_{n}}+6{x}_{n}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{2{x}_{0}}+3{x}_{0}^{2}-2}{2{e}^{2{x}_{0}}+6{x}_{0}} \\  & =0.5-\frac{{e}^{2\cdot 0.5}+3\cdot {0.5}^{2}-2}{2{e}^{2\cdot 0.5}+6\cdot 0.5} \\  & ≈0.326,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

$$

$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{2}+{x}_{n}-3}{2{x}_{n}+1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(2{x}_{n}+1)-({x}_{n}^{2}+{x}_{n}-3)}{2{x}_{n}+1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}^{2}+3}{2{x}_{n}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{{x}_{0}^{2}+3}{2{x}_{0}+1} \\  & =\frac{(0.8)^{2}+3}{2(0.8)+1} \\  & =\frac{3.64}{2.6} \\  & =1.4.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$

\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{3{x}_{1}^{4}-1}{4{x}_{1}^{3}-2} \\  & =\frac{3(1.407\,608…)^{4}-1}{4(1.407\,608…)^{3}-2} \\  & ≈1.396,\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-1}{(\frac{1}{{x}_{n}})} \\  & ={x}_{n}-({x}_{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}) \\  & =2{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =2{x}_{0}-{x}_{0}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{0} \\  & =2(1.5)-(1.5)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(1.5) \\  & =2.391\,802….\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2{x}_{1}-{x}_{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{1} \\  & =2(2.391\,802…)-(2.391\,802…)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(2.391\,802…) \\  & =2.697\,840….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}≈2.392$ and ${x}_{2}≈2.698,$ rounded to three decimal places.

The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡x-2)^{′}=-\frac{1}{x}+1
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-2}{(-\frac{1}{{x}_{n}}+1)} \\  & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}({x}_{n}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-2)}{{x}_{n}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}({x}_{n}-1)-{x}_{n}({x}_{n}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}-2)}{{x}_{n}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{n}+1)}{{x}_{n}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{{x}_{0}(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{0}+1)}{{x}_{0}-1} \\  & =\frac{0.1\,(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.1)+1)}{0.1-1} \\  & =0.144…\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{{x}_{1}(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{1}+1)}{{x}_{1}-1} \\  & =\frac{0.144…(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.144…)+1)}{0.144⋯-1} \\  & =0.157…, \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{{x}_{2}(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}_{2}+1)}{{x}_{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{0.157…(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(0.157…)+1)}{0.157⋯-1} \\  & =0.158….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈0.16$ and ${x}_{3}≈0.16$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x≈0.16,$ rounded to two decimal places.

canonical_examples.problem: Suppose we wish to find a root of the function $f(x)=5^{2x}-20$ in the interval $[0,2].$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting from the point $x_0 = 1.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (5^{2x}-20)' = 2\ln (5)\cdot 5^{2x}.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{5}^{2{x}_{n}}-20}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot {5}^{2{x}_{n}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{5}^{2{x}_{0}}-20}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot {5}^{2{x}_{0}}}. \\  & =1-\frac{{5}^{2}-20}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot {5}^{2}}. \\  & ≈0.938,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

canonical_examples.problem: Suppose we wish to find a root of the function $f(x)=e^x-x^3-3$ in the interval $[4,6].$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting from the point $x_0 = 5.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (e^x-x^3-3)' = e^x-3x^2.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-{x}_{n}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-3{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-{x}_{0}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-3{x}_{0}^{2}} \\  & =5-\frac{{e}^{5}-{5}^{3}-3}{{e}^{5}-3(5)^{2}} \\  & =4.721\,941…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-{x}_{1}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-3{x}_{1}^{2}} \\  & =(4.721\,941…)-\frac{{e}^{4.721\,941…}-(4.721\,941…)^{3}-3}{{e}^{4.721\,941…}-3(4.721\,941…)^{2}} \\  & ≈4.632,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

canonical_examples.problem: Given that the function $f(x)=x^5-2$ has a root in the interval $[0,2],$ use the Newton-Raphson process starting from $x_0=1$ to estimate the root. Round your final answer to two decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (x^5-2)' = 5x^4.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{5}-2}{5{x}_{n}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(5{x}_{n}^{4})-({x}_{n}^{5}-2)}{5{x}_{n}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}_{n}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{n}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{4{x}_{0}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{0}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4(1)^{5}+2}{5(1)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{5} \\  & =1.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{4{x}_{1}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{1}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4(1.2)^{5}+2}{5(1.2)^{4}} \\  & =1.152… \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{4{x}_{2}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{2}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4(1.152…)^{5}+2}{5(1.152…)^{4}} \\  & =1.148….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations $x_2 \approx 1.15$ and $x_3 \approx 1.15$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x \approx 1.15,$ rounded to two decimal places.
